title: Al-Halim, the Forbearing
tomorrow: why do Muslims say 'magnificent' while bending low?

cards: Someone knocks a full drink onto the new couch at your party, and every head in the room turns. Not to the stain. To you.
What you do in the next three seconds is the whole story. Yesterday's question: a stranger does something shocking in the mosque, then what? Here's the scene.

A Bedouin, a man from the desert, walks into the mosque of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Medina, goes to a corner, and starts to relieve himself on the floor. The companions leap up, shouting at him to stop.

teach.b: …leave him. Don't interrupt him. They hold back.

teach.h: A BUCKET OF WATER, A QUIET WORD.
teach.b: When the man is done, the Prophet asks for a bucket of water and has it poured over the spot.
Then he calls the man over and explains, gently, that mosques aren't for this; they're for remembering Allah, for prayer, for the Qur'an.

And to his companions he says: you were sent to make things easy, not to make them hard. That's the detail to tell a friend tonight. The rebuke went to the people shouting, not to the man who'd messed up.
This is hilm, forbearance: the strength to wait before reacting, and today's Name comes from it.

Al-Halim, the Forbearing, slow to punish. The Qur'an says that if Allah took people to task right away for what they earn, He wouldn't leave a living creature on the earth, but He gives time. Slow doesn't mean careless.
It means room to turn around. In another hadith, the Prophet told a man from a visiting tribe that he had two qualities Allah loves: forbearance, and taking your time.
A bucket of water, a quiet word, and a man who walked out still welcome.

how: Muslims retell the story of the Bedouin in the mosque as a model for teaching gently; hilm, forbearance, is praised as a quality Allah loves.

o: the one who forgets what people do
the one who never minds wrongdoing

games.q: who did what in the mosque — tap the pairs.
p: leave him; bring a bucket of water

s: Al-Halim means God doesn't care what people do
He gives time, and slow isn't careless: it's room to turn around.
the Prophet's rebuke went to the shouting companions, not the man
you were sent to make things easy, he told them, not to make them hard.

games.q: your little brother tracks mud across the floor you just mopped, and laughs. what does the mosque story point to?
o: yell now, so he learns it the hard way.
say nothing, ever, and quietly mop it again.
breathe, clean it with him, then explain why it matters.
games.why: the Prophet let the man finish, had water poured, then explained gently. the mess got cleaned and the person stayed welcome.

practice: Rest both palms flat on your legs and keep them still. Bring to mind the person most likely to get under your skin this week.
Each time you feel yourself answering them in your head, leave your hands where they are and let one slow breath pass first.

wordCard.voice: Al-Halim. The Forbearing, slow to punish, who gives room to turn around.

orig.note: Arabic: the Forbearing, from hilm, the strength to wait before reacting.

carryVoice: The line to keep: forbearing, three seconds slower than the room, and still kind after. Peace till tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 220, 6128; Sahih Muslim 285 (the Bedouin in the mosque: leave him; a bucket of water; you were sent to make things easy)
Sahih Muslim 17 (al-Ashajj: two qualities Allah loves, forbearance and deliberateness)
Qur'an 35:45 (if Allah took people to task for what they earn, He would not leave a living creature; but He reprieves them)
